attempted_axis: resolve the unclaimed .sdata2 0x8 DATADIFF blocker on game/anim/anim_play, examined first through the dead-strip lens per the work claim, then through the per-TU int-to-double pool-literal lens with a Matching sibling as positive control

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.base-cast-reconstruction-deadstrips-sibling-statics.20260831.v1 SCREENED AND FALSIFIED for this TU - this is the verdict's central negative finding. That law's warning signature is a TU static datum with NO incoming relocation in its own object (a base-cast reconstruction having silently deleted its siblings from the link). Tested directly with `powerpc-eabi-objdump -r`: the 8-byte .sdata2 datum (pool symbol @794) carries THREE incoming R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 relocations at .text 0x83a, 0xc3e and 0x13ea, so it is not dead-strippable and the dead-strip lens does not apply. The blocker is not a reconstruction defect at all. claim.law.inline-and-deadstrip-rules.20260829.v1 screened for its sdata2 pool-ordering clause (literals first, then const objects) and used to reason about pool position; consistent with the finding. The winglobals pool-ordering guidance ('literal-address forms in Matching TUs are correct, never symbolify') screened and CONFIRMED in the opposite direction: anim_play's remaining pool literals are currently spelled as extern lbl_* reads, which is the NonMatching staging idiom, and they are the reason our object emits only ONE of the pool's fourteen doublewords.
attributes.residual: VERDICT: the blocker was a MISSING SPLIT CLAIM, not a code or reconstruction defect, and it is now RESOLVED. Evidence chain. (1) Our anim_play.o emits .sdata2 of exactly 0x8 bytes, align 2**3, contents 43300000 80000000 under compiler pool symbol @794 - the standard PowerPC int-to-double conversion magic 0x4330000080000000, emitted by MWCC for the signed-int-to-float conversions in GetAnimAngXYZVal and InitAnimInvDeltaTable. (2) It is referenced by three of our own relocations, so it is genuine required data. (3) In the DOL the same constant sits at VA 0x80345838, and the target's GetAnimAngXYZVal loads it there: `lfd f28,0(0) @lbl_80345838(EMB_SDA21)` at function offsets 0x66c and 0xa70, precisely where our stream loads @794. (4) POSITIVE CONTROL, decisive: the sibling TU game/anim/anim.c is already Matching, its object emits a byte-identical 8-byte .sdata2 holding the same magic constant at the same 2**3 alignment, and splits.txt claims exactly `.sdata2 start:0x803457C8 end:0x803457D0` for it - the DOL indeed holds 4330000080000000 at 0x803457C8. Each TU that performs an int-to-float conversion gets its own private copy of this constant in its own pool; anim.c's claim is the template and anim_play.c simply never received the equivalent line. (5) The region 0x803457D0-0x80345848 is a contiguous fourteen-doubleword anim_play pool (1.0, 0.5, 0.125, 0.0, pi, 2pi, -pi, +/-pi/2 and the magic), fully symbolized in symbols.txt as lbl_* and currently read from source as externs; the magic is the ONLY member MWCC generates rather than reads, because it is compiler-synthesized and cannot be spelled away. FIX APPLIED: added `.sdata2 start:0x80345838 end:0x80345840` to game/anim/anim_play.c in config/GUNE5D/splits.txt (commit 47992778a). datadiff now reports `.sdata2: OK 0x8 bytes compared` (byte-verified against the DOL, exit 0) and claimcheck reports ok; both previously failed. Matched Data rose 175672 -> 175680 bytes overall and 62556 -> 62564 in Game Code. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FLIP: the DATA half of the anim_play flip blocker is now clear, but the TU flip does NOT materialize, because the TEXT half is untouched - GetAnimAngXYZVal remains at real 172 / 1047 of 1047 instructions under the standing eleven-axis REGISTER_ONLY cap (attempt.getanimangxyzval-register-web-closure.20260829.v1), which was NOT re-litigated this session and remains the live forensic record and the sole remaining blocker. NOTE for whoever eventually flips this TU: claiming the remaining thirteen doublewords will additionally require replacing the extern lbl_* reads with real C literals so MWCC generates the whole pool in the target's order, with the magic landing last at 0x80345838.
